title: The Top 13 New Rich Mistakes
coreMove: Run a relapse audit whenever freedom opens: protect time from work for work's sake, overchecking, extra customers, blurred space, and lonely autonomy.

exampleSpecs.stakes: One quick answer may train the support system to depend on the owner again.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the 13 mistakes and outsourceable questions to expose work for work's sake.

exampleSpecs.audience: a solo operator whose home has become the office
exampleSpecs.stakes: Location freedom may blur every room into work unless the environment gets a boundary.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use coworking, home office, and coffee shop separation to protect social rewards.

exampleSpecs.audience: an owner watching a stable business dashboard
exampleSpecs.stakes: Excess checking may look like care while it rebuilds the owner's bottleneck.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show micromanaging as a relapse from the Top 13 mistakes checklist.

exampleSpecs.audience: a store owner choosing whether to scale ads
exampleSpecs.stakes: More customers may bring money while stealing the time the money was meant to buy.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Tie unnecessary customer chasing to enough income and lifestyle maintenance.

exampleSpecs.audience: a freelancer adjusting to a newly open schedule
exampleSpecs.stakes: An automated week may still feel poor if it cuts off friendship and love.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use social rewards as a required part of lifestyle maintenance.

exampleSpecs.audience: a product owner deciding whether to interrupt a day off
exampleSpecs.stakes: A small bug may become a respectable reason to return to unnecessary work.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show a minor problem turning into work for work's sake.
